_about: The truth hub (plan 7.6f), the third built after love and righteousness: it leads with the noun, as righteousness does. Rows as in love.json and righteousness.json: a noun row is the words standing in the noun's own phrase or verse, an adjective row the same for the adjective, a verb row the frame of the verb; 'in_verse' is a word anywhere in the verse, 'object_of' a verb whose object the concept's word is. A verse sits in every row it fits (match: all). Built by tools/concepts/hub_build.py into out/concept-hubs/truth.json. The committee flagged it low (committee-flags.json): אֱמֶת (reliability, faithfulness) and ἀλήθεια are pooled in one noun form, and 'the Spirit of truth' stands close to disputes about the Spirit's procession; kept as that note asks -- each phrase as written, no gloss on the Spirit's relation to the Father or the Son. First built with 49 rows; consolidated to about 25 (coordinator, rule 8: 15-25 rows, never 40+): companion rows of a handful of verses joined a broader row, small rows went to the catch-all, nothing was dropped from the hub's verses. Where the first build kept Hebrew and Greek companions in rows of their own, they now share a row and every example names its word.
_words_why: The concept's own words: אֱמֶת and Aramaic קְשֹׁט (Dan 4:37, 'all His works are true'), ἀλήθεια, ἀληθής and ἀληθινός (two Greek words the Berean prints 'true'; each example names the one its verse uses) and the verb ἀληθεύω (2 verses). The adverb ἀληθῶς ('truly', 18 verses) is the same family but the builder's forms are noun, adjective and verb, and an adverb would be filed as an adjective (the pos letter 'A' of 'ADV'), under rows that say 'called true'; it is left to the section of other words, where it shows beside ἀμήν, which is a different word. אֱמוּנָה and אָמַן (faithfulness, believe) are the same Hebrew root but the faith concept's words, and the Berean renders אֱמוּנָה 'truth' only 6 times of 49.
_sense_why: אֱמֶת is one Hebrew word the Berean prints 'truth' (37), 'faithfulness' (41), 'true' (19) and 'faithful', 'faithfully', 'good faith', 'truthful', 'trustworthy', 'reliable', 'faith' (about 18 more): all counted, because the Hebrew gives no second word for them, and a hub that kept only the 'truth' verses would show a Hebrew word as less than it is. Left out, as another sense of the word, are the 10 verses where the Berean prints 'security' (2 Kgs 20:19, Isa 39:8, Jer 33:6), 'sure' (Josh 2:12, Ps 132:11, Ps 69:14 -- 'sure salvation'), 'lasting' (Jer 14:13), 'purest' (Jer 2:21), 'fairness' (Prov 29:14) and 'right' (Gen 24:48): there the verse does not show truth or faithfulness. ἀληθινός Heb 10:22 ('a sincere heart') is left out for the same reason. 'real' keeps ἀληθής at Acts 12:9 ('what the angel was doing was real'); 'surety' is MACULA's gloss for the Aramaic at Dan 2:47, where the Berean prints 'Truly'.

others._why: As in love.json: the rows stand on the concept's own words; other Greek and Hebrew words the Berean also renders 'true' or 'truly' (ἀμήν 'truly I tell you', ὄντως, and the adverb ἀληθῶς) are named apart, each with its verses, and never handed over as the same word.
others.title: Other words translated “true” and “truly”

rows.label: Loving devotion and faithfulness

not_verses.Zech.7.9: 'true justice' and, in the next phrase, 'loving devotion': the Hebrew has אֱמֶת with מִשְׁפָּט here, not beside חֶסֶד

rows.note: The Hebrew pair is חֶסֶד and אֱמֶת. The Berean prints the second "faithfulness" in some verses and "truth" in others; it is one Hebrew word, kept as printed. The Berean prints חֶסֶד "loving devotion", "kindness" or "mercy". Another Hebrew word, אֱמוּנָה, is also printed "faithfulness"; it is not in this hub. ἀλήθεια in the Greek rows is a different word, and each example names the word its verse uses.
rows._why: panel: led with verses that print 'loving devotion' (Gen 24:27 prints 'kindness'). Committee: 'keep each phrase as written'. Label in the Berean's own words for this pair (Exod 34:6, Ps 85:10); a label saying 'truth' would not show in the 41 verses that print 'faithfulness'

rows.label: Truth or faithfulness beside justice, righteousness, judgment and peace

not_verses.Jer.28.9: 'peace' is what the prophet prophesies; 'comes true' and 'truly sent' are not beside it
not_verses.Rom.3.7: κρίνω is 'condemned as a sinner' in the Berean; the verse is in the row of God's truth

rows.note: Two different words: Hebrew אֱמֶת (the Berean prints it "truth", "faithfulness" or "true") and Greek ἀλήθεια; each example names its word.
rows._why: panel (14 fixes): relabelled and led with verses that print 'truth' or 'true'; the note had been build history ('the first build kept them in two rows'), now a reader's note. Merged from 'Truth, justice, righteousness and peace' (Hebrew) and 'Truth and righteousness, judgment' (Greek)

rows.label: The truth of the LORD, of God; the true God
rows.note: The text's own phrase, kept as written ("the God of truth", "the faithfulness of the LORD", "the true God"), with no gloss on whose or which Person.
rows._why: the phrase rule of the righteousness hub (adjacent: true = the very next word either side); the divine persons are not inferred -- a phrase that names Him is the text's. 'אֵל' added to the divine set for Ps 31:5 'God of truth'
rows._add_why: Jer 10:10 'the LORD is the true God' (the first build's row 'The true God'): the clause puts אֱמֶת after אֱלֹהִים in a separate part the next-word window does not cross

rows.label: “Your truth,” “Your faithfulness,” said to the LORD, to God
rows._why: by hand, as the divine persons are: 'Your' said to Him, in verses that themselves name the LORD or God (Ps 40:11 'O LORD', Ps 71:22 'O my God', Ps 86:11 'O LORD', Ps 86:15 'O Lord', Ps 115:1 'O LORD', Ps 25:5 'the God of my salvation', Dan 9:13 'the LORD our God'). Panel: Ps 119:151 ('all Your commandments are true') removed -- it does not contain the quoted words, and stands in the law and justice rows. Gen 32:10 ('all the kindness and faithfulness You have shown Your servant') added: it is Jacob's prayer, one sentence with Gen 32:9, which names 'the LORD'; the word is absent from the built occurrences of אֱמֶת (a gap in the data: 124 rows for 127 uses), so no rule can see it and it is placed by hand. Psalms that say 'Your truth' without naming Him in the verse (Ps 26:3, 43:3, 57:10, 108:4, 138:2) are left to the rows they fit, as righteousness left Rev 15:3

rows.label: The Spirit of truth; the Spirit is the truth
rows.note: The text's own phrases, kept as written (John 15:26 adds "who proceeds from the Father"); where Christian traditions part on how the Spirit relates to the Father and the Son, the page takes no side.
rows._add_why: 1 John 5:6 'the Spirit is the truth', by hand: the verse names the Spirit (the first build's one-verse row)

rows.label: Worship in spirit and in truth
Truth said of Christ, of Jesus
rows._why: panel: Rom 9:1 removed (Paul's oath, 'I speak the truth in Christ'; the truth is Paul's speech, not said of Christ; it stands in the speak-the-truth row). By hand, as the divine persons are: verses where the text itself names the Word, Christ or Jesus beside the truth (John 1:14 'the Word ... full of grace and truth', 1:17 'through Jesus Christ', 14:6 'I am ... the truth' -- Jesus is speaking, 18:37 'Jesus answered', 2 Cor 11:10 'the truth of Christ', Eph 4:21 'the truth is in Jesus'); no gloss added

rows.label: Walk in the truth, the way and the truth

not_verses.1John.1.6: 'walk in the darkness' -- the walking is not in the truth
not_verses.2Sam.15.20: הָלַךְ is 'I go where I may', not walking in truth
not_verses.Gen.24.27: דֶּרֶךְ here is the journey ('led me on the journey'), not the way of truth

rows._why: merged from 'Walk in the truth' and 'The way and the truth'

rows.label: Speak the truth, tell it, do it, show faithfulness
rows._why: merged from 'Speak the truth, tell the truth' and 'Show, do, practice the truth': both are verbs whose object is the truth

rows.label: Knowing the truth: knowledge, wisdom, instruction

not_verses.Prov.22.21: 'to teach you true and reliable words': the truth is the words' quality, not what is known
not_verses.John.14.17: the world 'knows' the Spirit, not the truth; the verse is in the Spirit row
not_verses.1John.4.6: 'we know the Spirit of truth': the Spirit is known, not the truth; in the Spirit row
not_verses.1John.2.4: 'I know Him' -- the One known is not the truth
not_verses.1John.3.19: what is known is that we belong to the truth, not the truth itself
not_verses.Col.1.6: ἐπιγινώσκω is 'understood the grace of God'; the truth is how, not what
not_verses.Isa.38.19: יָדַע here is 'tell' (make known) Your faithfulness to children
not_verses.Jer.26.15: יָדַע is 'know for certain that if you put me to death'
not_verses.Jer.28.9: 'recognized as one the LORD has truly sent'
not_verses.1Kgs.10.6: the report about the king's wisdom is called true; wisdom is not beside the truth but what the report is about
not_verses.Dan.10.1: 'understanding of the message' follows 'the message was true'; they are not beside each other

rows.note: In the New Testament phrase "the knowledge of the truth" (1 Tim 2:4, 2 Tim 2:25, Heb 10:26, Titus 1:1), Christian traditions part on whom God wills to save, how one comes to it, and whether it can be lost; the page takes no side.
rows._why: merged from 'Know the truth', 'The knowledge of the truth' and 'Wisdom, knowledge, instruction and the truth'. οἶδα is not in the list (it is 'know that' in most verses)

rows.label: Truth beside faith, obedience and love

not_verses.1John.3.19: πείθω is 'assure' here ('assure our hearts'), not 'obey'

rows.note: In the New Testament verses, Christian traditions part on what faith is, how it is given, how God's choosing stands to it, and how it stands to obedience and love; the page takes no side.
rows._add_why: 1 Cor 13:6 ('Love ... rejoices in the truth'): the Greek has no word for 'love' in the verse itself (it is the subject carried over from 13:4), so the in-verse rule cannot see it
rows._why: merged from 'Truth and faith', 'Obeying the truth, refusing to obey it' and 'Truth and love'

rows.label: Truth and its opposites: the lie, wickedness, deception; turning from it; truth missing
rows._add_why: by hand: the verses that say truth is lacking, a short list the text itself gives (Isa 59:14 'truth has stumbled', 59:15 'Truth is missing', Dan 8:12 'flung truth to the ground', Hos 4:1 'There is no truth'); 1 John 1:8 'the truth is not in us' (πλανάω is 'deceive ourselves' there, so the rule on straying cannot own it)
rows._why: merged from 'Turned from, strayed from, opposed, suppressed, exchanged for a lie', 'Truth and the lie, falsehood', 'Truth, wickedness and deception', 'Truth missing, stumbled, flung down' and 'The truth is not in him, not in us'. ἀποστερέω stays out (1 Tim 6:5 'devoid of the truth' says a state, not something done to the truth). The Berean prints ἀδικία 'evil', 'wickedness'; πλάνη 'deception'

rows.label: “Your word is truth”, the word of truth, the truth of the gospel

not_verses.2Chr.32.1: דְּבָרִים here is 'acts' ('these acts of faithfulness'), not words
not_verses.Ps.45.4: דָּבָר here is 'the cause' ('for the cause of truth')

rows.note: In the New Testament phrases (Eph 1:13, Col 1:5, Jas 1:18, John 17:17), readers take "the word" of Scripture, of Christ or of the gospel; the page does not choose.
rows._add_why: by hand: shapes the next-word window cannot see -- the word and the truth in different parts (Jer 23:28 'speak My word faithfully'); the word as subject, truth as predicate (John 17:17, 1 Kgs 17:24, 2 Sam 7:28, Dan 10:1 'the message was true', Ps 119:160 'the entirety of Your word is truth', whose subject head is 'entirety'); and Gal 2:5, 2:14 'the truth of the gospel'. Panel: Gen 42:16 (Joseph testing his brothers' words), 1 Kgs 10:6 and 2 Chr 9:5 (the Queen of Sheba's report), Esth 9:30 (Mordecai's letters) are human words, not God's, and left this row (they stand in the catch-all and the justice row); the label now leads with the Hebrew Scripture's own claim and the note is scoped to the New Testament phrases
rows._why: merged from 'The word of truth', 'The word is truth, the message is true' and 'The truth of the gospel'

rows.label: Set free, sanctified, purified, guided by the truth
rows.note: Where Christian traditions part on how sanctification and purifying come about, and what part obedience has in them, the page takes no side.
rows._why: panel: note added. By hand: the verses that name what the truth does; John 16:13 is the Spirit of truth guiding

rows.label: The truth that abides in us, that we now have
rows._why: panel (missing verse): 2 John 1:2 ('because of the truth that abides in us and will be with us forever') was in no row, not even the catch-all: the clause that holds it starts at 1:1, and the builder files a clause under the first verse where the word stands, so 1:2 was never seen. A pick is the only way to place it; 2 Pet 1:12 ('established in the truth you now have') is the one other verse that says the truth is held, taken out of the catch-all to make the row

rows.label: Truth and the law, commandments

not_verses.Titus.1.14: 'the commands of men who have rejected the truth' are men's commands, not God's law; placed here it reads as if the commandments stand against the truth. The verse stays in the row of turning from the truth

rows.note: In John 1:17, Rom 2:20 and similar New Testament verses, Christian traditions part on the law and the gospel; the page takes no side.
rows._why: panel: led with the Hebrew Scriptures' own words about their law ('Your law is true', 'true laws', 'True instruction'); note scoped to the New Testament verses; Titus 1:14 removed

rows.label: In truth, truly, faithfully
rows.note: Hebrew בְּ or Greek ἐν / ἐπί beside the word for truth; where the Berean prints "certainly", "in fact" or "correctly" (Luke 22:59, Acts 4:27, Mark 12:32) it renders the same phrase.

not_verses.1Kgs.22.16: בְּ here is 'in the name of the LORD', after 'nothing but the truth'
not_verses.Dan.9.13: 'giving attention to Your truth': the בְּ is not 'in truth'
not_verses.Rom.2.2: 'is based on truth' (κατά): the ἐπί in the clause is with another word
not_verses.John.17.17: the Berean prints 'by the truth'; it has a row of its own
not_verses.Rom.1.18: 'in unrighteousness' follows the truth: ἐν is with ἀδικία
not_verses.Rom.2.20: 'in the law': ἐν is with νόμος
not_verses.Eph.6.14: 'belt of truth': ἐν is with the belt
not_verses.John.8.44: 'stand in the truth': the Berean prints 'refusing to uphold the truth'
not_verses.Col.1.5: 'in the word of truth': ἐν is with λόγος

rows._why: merged from the Hebrew and the Greek 'in truth' rows

rows.label: Every other use
rows._why: the catch-all now also holds what the first build's small rows held and no larger row takes: 'Truth and the light', 'Truth and the heart', 'Grace and truth', 'Testimony, witness and the truth', 'The belt of truth' (Eph 6:14, in the row of righteousness) and '"What is truth?"' (John 18:38); the doors to the belt and to Pilate's question stay here

rows.label: The true light, the true bread, the true vine, the true worshipers
rows._add_why: John 6:32 'the true bread from heaven': the Greek puts the adjective after a clause break the next-word window does not cross
rows.note: Two Greek words are here, ἀληθής and ἀληθινός; each example names the one its verse uses.

rows.label: Testimony, words, ways and judgments called true; “faithful and true”

not_verses.Matt.22.16: 'the way of God' is taught 'in accordance with the truth' in the speakers' flattery; the ways are not called true
not_verses.Luke.16.11: 'faithful with worldly wealth' and 'true riches' are two things
not_verses.1Pet.5.12: 'a faithful brother' and 'the true grace of God' are two things
not_verses.Rom.3.4: 'Let God be true ... when You speak' says God is true; it is in the God-is-true row

rows.note: Two Greek words are printed "true": ἀληθής (truthful) and ἀληθινός (genuine, real); each example names its word. Testimony is called true (John 19:35) and "not valid" (John 5:31) as the text has it, side by side; the Berean prints the same Greek word ἀληθής "valid" in John 5:31-32, 8:13-14 and 8:17.
rows._add_why: said, not a noun for speech: John 10:41 'everything John said ... was true', John 4:18 'You have spoken truthfully' (a rule on λέγω would take every verse of dialogue)
rows._why: merged from 'Testimony, witness: true, or not true', 'True ways, true judgments', 'Faithful and true' and 'Words, sayings said to be true'

rows.label: God is true; “the only true God”, “the living and true God”
rows.note: Two Greek words are printed "true": ἀληθής (truthful, John 3:33, Rom 3:4) and ἀληθινός (genuine, real: John 17:3, 1 Thess 1:9, Rev 6:10); each example names its word.

rows.label: “Him who is true”, “the true God”
